newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates broadly stable in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates broadly stable in quiet market.

text.p: Greek depo rates were little changed in late trade but for some upward bias in short rates and the central bank soaked overnight funds at 12.40 percent with market liquidity balancing out, traders said.

"Depos are stable with a tendency for slightly higher levels," said a dealer at a state bank. "Liquidity must be balancing out at current levels although the central bank drained overnight funds at an unchanged 12.40 percent."
The dealer estimated market liquidity at plus/minus 50 billion drachmas and added that the Bank of Greece checked bank positions throughout the day.
Other dealers said short rates could head higher as some players sought to fund Monday's T-bill purchases.
T-bill sales exceeded maturities by about 100 billion drachmas draining more liquidity on Monday, dealers said.
T-bill sales amounted to over 750 billion drachmas, press reports said.
No official figures were available as T-bills renewals could continue even today.
Early elections are to be held on September 22 but the market has taken a positive attitude towards them on the belief the winner will have no option but to follow Greece's EU convergence plan.
The mark was quoted at 159.55/60 drachmas from Tuesday's 159.610 fix, the dollar at 237.55/65 drachmas from 237.360 and the Ecu at 301.01/11 from 301.170 drachmas.
